title: The Guardian Angels (2 October)
hookLine: a knock at the gate, a servant girl, and a room that says: it is his angel

cards: Night in Jerusalem. A house full of people praying for Peter, who is in prison. Knocking at the outer gate.
A servant girl named Rhoda goes to answer, hears Peter's voice, and is so overjoyed she runs back inside without opening the gate. Peter's out there, she tells them. They say she's mad.
She insists. And then they say something strange, in the Douay-Rheims: "It is his angel." Meanwhile Peter keeps knocking.

teach.h: THE BELIEVERS GUESS: IT IS HIS ANGEL.
teach.b: That scene in Acts is funny, and it's also a window. When Rhoda insists Peter is at the gate, the believers' first guess isn't a ghost or a mistake. It's his angel.
They took for granted that a person might have an angel of his own. Catholics build on that, and on a line from Jesus himself.

teach.h: THEIR ANGELS SEE THE FACE OF MY FATHER.
teach.b: In Matthew, he sets a child in front of the disciples and says, in the Douay-Rheims: "See that you despise not one of these little ones: for I say to you, that their angels in heaven always see the face of my Father who is in heaven."
Even the smallest, the ones adults overlook, have someone in God's presence on their behalf.
Psalm ninety, in the Douay-Rheims numbering, says it as a promise: "For he hath given his angels charge over thee; to keep thee in all thy ways."
From those threads comes the long Catholic tradition that each person has an angel, a guardian, given by God to watch over them through life.
The Church keeps a feast for them on the second of October, a few days after the archangels.

teach.h: NOT A CHARM: A COMPANION AT YOUR SIDE.
teach.b: Notice what a guardian angel is not: not a pet spirit, not a lucky charm, not someone you become when you die. In Catholic teaching, angels are their own kind of creature.

teach.h: TO KEEP THEE IN ALL THY WAYS.
teach.b: The guardian's job is quiet: to stay close, and to keep turning a person toward God. That's why the old children's prayer to the guardian angel asks it to light, guard, rule and guide. Not to perform.

how: The memorial of the Holy Guardian Angels is kept on 2 October; Catholic children are taught a short prayer to their guardian angel, the Angele Dei, to say in the morning and at night.

games.why: Acts says she was so glad she didn't open the gate; she ran in, and the others said it is his angel.

practice: Think back over a stretch of your life and notice one moment when something kept you: a near miss, the right person at the right time, a voice in your head that said wait.

If you pray, thank your guardian angel for that moment, plainly, the way a child might; if you don't, just notice that you were kept, and give thanks, if you like, to whoever or whatever was beside you.

wordCard.voice: Messenger, what the Greek word angel means. In Catholic teaching, the guardian angel God gives each person stays close and keeps turning them toward God.

orig.note: the Greek word behind angel in the New Testament; it means a messenger.

carryVoice: Your line: beside you. Not a charm, but a companion who stays. Rest well.
